## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # geo spatial
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Geospatial shapes and poses
//  - Geospatial terrain and rasters
//  - Geospatial reference systems

//==
// # Geospatial shapes and poses
//
// Regions, paths, and shapes drawn on a planet's surface, plus the headings and
// vehicle poses expressed against it. Positions are geodetic coordinates
// (GeoCoordinate); angles are Angle and distances are Length.

//==
// # Regions, paths, and shapes

// A latitude-longitude aligned region: the latitude band [South, North] and
// the longitude band traveling eastward from West to East. West greater than
// East encodes a region crossing the antimeridian.
type GeoBounds
    implements IGeoRegion
{
    South: Angle;
    North: Angle;
    West: Angle;
    East: Angle;
}

// An ordered sequence of geodetic coordinates: a route, a track, or a
// polygon ring. Consecutive coordinates are joined by geodesic segments.
type GeoPath
{
    Coordinates: Array<GeoCoordinate>;
}

// A polygonal region on the planet's surface: an outer boundary ring plus
// zero or more hole rings. Rings are implicitly closed (last coordinate joins
// the first); the boundary winds counter-clockwise seen from above, holes
// clockwise.
type GeoPolygon
    implements IGeoRegion
{
    Boundary: GeoPath;
    Holes: Array<GeoPath>;
}

// The shortest (great-circle, or geodesic on the ellipsoid) arc between two
// geodetic coordinates.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great-circle_distance)
type GeoSegment
    implements IValue
{
    Start: GeoCoordinate;
    End: GeoCoordinate;
}

// A circular region on the planet's surface: all points within a geodesic
// distance Radius of Center, measured along the surface.
type GeoCircle
    implements IGeoRegion
{
    Center: GeoCoordinate;
    Radius: Length;
}

//==
// # Headings and poses

// A navigation heading measured clockwise from true north.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bearing_(navigation))
type CompassBearing
    implements IValue
{
    Angle: Angle;
}

// The placement of a vehicle or sensor on the planet: geodetic position plus
// heading (clockwise from true north), pitch (positive nose-up), and roll
// (positive right-wing-down).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_principal_axes)
type GeoPose
    implements IValue
{
    Position: GeoCoordinate;
    Heading: CompassBearing;
    Pitch: Angle;
    Roll: Angle;
}

//==
// # Geospatial terrain and rasters
//
// Gridded planet data and the addressing that ties raster pixels to ground:
// elevation grids, the pixel-to-projected-coordinate mapping of a north-up
// image, and slippy-map tile addresses. Distances are Length.

// A regular grid of terrain elevations over a geographic region. Elevations
// are in meters above the datum's reference surface; the column index runs
// west to east and the row index runs south to north across Bounds.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_elevation_model)
type ElevationGrid
{
    Bounds: GeoBounds;
    Elevations: Array2D<Number>;
}

// The mapping from raster pixel indices to projected map coordinates for a
// north-up image: the easting/northing of the outer corner of the top-left
// (northwest) pixel, plus the positive pixel footprint. Easting grows by
// PixelWidth per column; northing shrinks by PixelHeight per row.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_file)
type GeoTransform
    implements IValue
{
    OriginEasting: Length;
    OriginNorthing: Length;
    PixelWidth: Length;
    PixelHeight: Length;
}

// The address of one tile in the XYZ (slippy map) pyramid: zoom level 0 is a
// single world tile; each level doubles the tile count per axis. Row 0 is the
// northernmost row.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiled_web_map)
type MapTileIndex
    implements IValue, IHashable
{
    Zoom: Integer;
    Column: Integer;
    Row: Integer;
}

//==
// # Geospatial reference systems
//
// The reference frames geodetic positions are expressed against: ellipsoids and
// datums, map projections and their grid zones, and the Cartesian coordinate
// systems used to compute with them. Angles are Angle; distances are Length.

//==
// # Datums and reference ellipsoids

// An oblate spheroid model of the planet used as a geodetic reference:
// equatorial semi-major axis plus the dimensionless inverse flattening
// (a / (a - b); WGS84 uses 298.257223563).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_ellipsoid)
type ReferenceEllipsoid
    implements IValue
{
    SemiMajorAxis: Length;
    InverseFlattening: Number;
}
```
